report.source_text: In the ectoscopic evaluation, significant facial asymmetry was observed, with obvious bulging in the right maxillary region, causing a slight distortion of the facial contour (Fig. 1a and b). Oroscopic examination revealed a pronounced swelling in the posterior area of the right maxilla, with a smooth surface, erythema and slight expansion of the hard palate, as well as hyperemia of the mucosa (Fig. 1c and d). Intraoral inspection revealed no superficial ulcerations, but the internal bulging suggested an underlying expansive process.

report.source_text: Cone beam computed tomography was performed for a more detailed assessment. Figure 2a and b show an expansive mass affecting the posterior region of the right maxilla, extending to the base of the maxillary sinus. The lesion shows heterogeneous areas with varying density, suggesting mixed lytic and sclerotic components, characteristic of aggressive lesions. The presence of bone destruction is evident, with compromised bone margins and involvement of adjacent structures, indicating invasive behavior of the mass. The mass is also visible in Fig. 2c and d, causing alterations to the bone contour and invading adjacent tissues. Significant erosion of the right maxillary bone can be seen, with areas of mixed density. The irregular density of the tumor suggests the production of osteoid matrix. The extension of the lesion beyond the primary bone structures reinforces the aggressive and infiltrative nature of the lesion.

report.source_text: There is an intense proliferation of small, round cells with a monotonous appearance, distributed in a dense and disorganized manner. These cells have a hyperchromatic nucleus and scarce cytoplasm, reinforcing the undifferentiated nature of the neoplasm. In addition, there are areas where the stroma is mineralized, with the presence of irregularly arranged bone matrix formation, a fundamental feature for the diagnosis of osteosarcoma, as it indicates direct production of osteoid matrix by the tumour cells. Another notable feature is the infiltrative aspect of the lesion, with tumor cells invading and breaking through the adjacent tissue architecture, without defined boundaries. This behavior suggests aggressiveness and is consistent with the malignant nature of osteosarcoma.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 8-year-old female presented with progressive right maxillofacial swelling, causing facial asymmetry, local discomfort, and difficulty chewing. Physical examination showed right maxillary swelling with mucosal erythema and palatal expansion without ulceration. Imaging with cone beam CT revealed an expansive, mixed lytic and sclerotic lesion of the right maxilla with bone destruction and osteoid matrix production, indicating an aggressive lesion consistent with osteosarcoma. An incisional biopsy was performed due to suspicion of malignancy. Immunohistochemistry showed high Ki-67 proliferation index and CD34 positivity, signaling aggressive behavior. Histopathology slides after surgical resection demonstrated classic small cell osteosarcoma features with intense proliferation of small, round, hyperchromatic cells and scarce cytoplasm. There was mineralized stroma with irregular bone matrix formation confirming direct osteoid production by tumor cells and an infiltrative pattern consistent with malignant osteosarcoma.
